pr_title: test: arch: arm: arm_interrupt: clear FPSCR register in ISR
pr_body:
test: arch: arm: arm_interrupt: clear FPSCR register in ISR

Clear Floating Point Status and Control Register (FPSCR),
in case FPU IRQ is selected by the test as "Available IRQ line"

Fixes #31982
pr_comments:
Note: I am not sure about the switches used.
Other switches may be more appropriate.

Though the current PR seems to fix your issue, @ABOSTM , for a proper fix for FPU_SHARING in this test, we also need to get #32041 in. We could do this post 2.5.0 release if @nashif does not want to merge that now. I've not noticed any failures of this test in cortex-m platforms so #32041 could wait, perhaps

issue_context.title: tests: kernel: queue: regression introduced by FPU sharing PR #31772
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Following tests:
* tests/kernel/queue/kernel.queue
* tests/arch/arm/arm_interrupt/arch.interrupt.arm
* tests/arch/arm/arm_interrupt/arch.interrupt.extra_exception_info
* tests/arch/arm/arm_interrupt/arch.interrupt.no_optimizations

are now failed on stm32f3_disco.
This is a regression introduced by PR #31772, test is passed before this PR and failed after.
Error message is not the same depending on test,
but in one case I got stack overflow. So I tried to enlarge MAIN_STACK_SIZE to 2048. It doesn't help.
I also increase IDLE_STACK_SIZE, ISR_STACK_SIZE and SYSTEM_WORKQUEUE_STACK_SIZE
but test is still failed.
Note: I could not reproduce issue on windows, only reproduced on Linux (different toolchain)


**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. twister -N --device-testing --hardware-map ../map.yaml -c  -p stm32f3_disco -T tests/kernel/queue/
2. See error

test passed

comments: There's probably some other thread that overflows, e.g. the ZTEST thread. I can take a look.

@ABOSTM I've tried the test on other cortex-m platforms (building with FPU_SHARING=y), I don't see stack overflows, so I can't help much with debugging, since i don't have this ST board.
You could find out the thread that overflows - if you build with THREAD_NAME support.
Then, as I mentioned, might be the ZTEST thread that overflows, you can increase
CONFIG_ZTEST_STACKSIZE and CONFIG_TEST_EXTRA_STACKSIZE to see if the overflows disappear.

@ioannisg,
Ok I will do so. Thanks for the hints.
